Posted September 17, 2003
Analysis by Richard Cowan

First, the good news.

Perhaps the best news is that Initiative 75 easily won in Seattle with 59% of the votes, making adult marijuana possession the lowest priority for the city police. As its opponents kept insisting, it probably will not make a lot of difference in actual police practice, because the Seattle police have been largely ignoring marijuana use.

However, it is politically very important. It puts the people of Seattle on record against arresting marijuana users. I75 was opposed by both of the city's dailies, which was reason enough to vote for it.

Rather comically, a Seattle Times editorial commented today, Sometimes, public sentiment moves more rapidly on social issues than elected officials. It appears to have done that via Initiative 75.

Yes, and sometimes, public sentiment ignores prohibitionist newspaper editors, too.
See
Letter to the Editors of the Seattle Times. Someone Is Lying to You. Supporters Of Cannabis Prohibition Need to Do A Credibility Check.

Congratulations to Dominic Holden, chairman of the The Sensible Seattle Coalition, which sponsored I-75, raised just over $150,000 and sent out three voter mailings to more than 70,000 Seattle residents. (Dominic is also the Director of the Seattle Hempfest, President of Washington NORML, and one of the marijuana reform movement's most effective young leaders.)
For his own account of recent events see
Czar Wars: The White House Lectures Seattle on Pot Initiative

Recently, John Walters made a stop in Seattle on his summer reefer madness tour, and naturally he opposed I75. A great article by Philip Dowdy in the Seattle Weekly noted Seattle media also missed a shift in the pot war. You had to listen hard, but it was there: Deep in his remarks about I-75, Walters made an admission you wouldn't have heard from federal drug enforcement officials even during the Clinton administration.

The real issue is should we legalize marijuana, Walters said. Let's have a debate about that.

Ever since the 1930s and propaganda films such as Reefer Madness, the feds have waged a multibillion-dollar war on marijuana use. Rarely have they acknowledged that millions of Americans actually like pot and use it responsibly, let alone that there might be a need for a national debate on how America should treat marijuana under the law.

As Dowdy observed, this really would be a major shift in prohibitionist tactics, and the rest of the Seattle media completely missed it. In fact, this morning's Seattle television news and the papers gave much more coverage to the defeat of a proposed tax on lattes than to the public's overwhelming opposition to arresting marijuana users. Pathetic.

Meanwhile in Canada

Moving on up the coast, British Columbia Provincial Court judge ruled that there is no offence known to law at this time for simple possession of marihuana.

However, it is not really binding, because the Provincial Court's rulings are subject to appeal by the Crown, and another case has actually been heard by the Canadian Supreme Court, which is expected to rule around the first of the year.

In any case, this probably will not make much difference, because the Vancouver police generally are not arresting people for possession. However, the Vancouver Police insisted that they still had the authority to arrest if they really, really want to, and then made complete fools of themselves by holding a news conference with the U.S. Consul General Luis Arreaga as their guest of honor. Of course, he warned that this could cause delays at the border Does Canada actually pay its police to undermine its sovereignty and subvert its Constitution?
See
Canada Exports A Little Reefer to DEAland. Imports A Lot of Reefer Madness. A Bad Balance of Trade. Canadian Taxpayers Are Being Lied to At Their Own Expense, But It May Also Cost Them Their Freedom.

The Judge's ruling simply reinforced the Ontario courts rulings that Health Canada's failure to provide a realistic medical marijuana program voided the possession laws.
See
Ontario Judge Prods Canadian Government On Medical Cannabis Program. Supreme Court Hearings On All Cannabis Prohibition Now Set For May. We Are Winning!

This week that failure took on almost comic elements. Philippe Lucas of the Victoria Compassion Society and Canadians for Safe Access attacked the poor quality of the diluted cannabis that Health Canada has tried to foist off on the patients. They started out with excellent weed, but diluted it because the prohibitionist ignoramuses at Health Canada decided that it was too strong! Now the patients even want their money back.
See
Canadian Health Minister Seeks Asylum In DEAland; Says Making Her Think About Medical Cannabis Constitutes Torture. In DC They Don't Allow That Sort of Thing. Thinking, That Is.

Meanwhile back the future in Alaska The Alaska Court of Appeals has ruled that adults have the right to possess less than four ounces of marijuana in their home for personal use. It just reaffirmed the 1975 Alaska Supreme Court case of Ravin v. State. That has really been the law all along, even though a 1990 ballot initiative supported by the Federal government under then-Drug Czar, Bet-A-Million Bennett, criminalized possession of any amount. That initiative passed with 55% of the vote, but did not amend the Alaska State Constitution, which has a very broad right to privacy.

Now, Alaska Attorney General Gregg Renkes says that state troopers and local police should try to federalize these cases. That is a betrayal of his oath to uphold the state constitution, and the Feds simply don't have the resources to try four-ounce possession cases.

Meanwhile, in San Diego

On a 6-3 vote, the San Diego City Council passed an ordinance on September 16th that clarifies the rules under which patients can grow their own medical marijuana. The ordinance allows a patient to possess a pound of processed marijuana and up to 24 unharvested plants. A caregiver would be allowed to keep up to 48 unharvested plants and could have as much as two pounds of the processed drug. Only indoor cultivation would be permitted; public growing and smoking isnot allowed. Patient will be issued a verification card with the name of the cardholder, a serial number, cardholder's photo and card expiration date.

Donald Thornhill, a special agent with the Drug Enforcement Administration in San Diego, told the City Council, " It really amounts to de facto legalization of drugs There is no medical use for marijuana -- none whatsoever. Period. It's nothing more than drug legalization. " The voters don't believe the DEA, and even the politicians are learning.
See
Walters Puts The Media to the Test By Taking Hyper-Lying to A New Level. Blood Libels To Justify Police State. San Diego Medical Activist Faces Federal Charges for 20 Plants.

Good or bad news??

It seems increasingly unlikely that the Canadian Parliament will get around to its phoney decrim bill this year. It would be far better if they did nothing, at least until the Canadian Supreme Court rules on all of the marijuana prohibition laws.
See
D oh! Canada? Proposed Marijuana Modernization Equals The Sum of All Their Ignorance. The Intellectual and Moral Bankruptcy of Canadian Cannabis Prohibition. Analysis by Richard Cowan

On the other hand, it would appear that the UK government is going ahead with its on phoney decrim bill around the first of the year. As MarijuanaNews has reported, it will reclassify cannabis, but leave the police the discretion to decide whether or not to arrest users. It will also raise penalties for growers, as would the Canadian modernization but in the UK they might just enforce the longer sentences, even though its prisons are more overcrowded than those in Canada.
See
UK Committee Will Endorse Reclassification " Decriminalization " By Another Name, But Says Real " Decriminalization " Would " Send the Wrong Message " Cannabis Equals Valium Is The Right Message?

The good news in this is that it is being widely reported in the media that cannabis use has been decriminalized, or even legalized in the UK.

" We are the European champions for cannabis consumption among the young, " said Interior Minister Nicolas Sarkozy Monday. Last year, The Guardian reported that Sarkozy has said that " The words 'soft' and 'drugs' will always be incompatible. There is quite simply no such thing as a 'soft drug'. We are determined to fight against drug dealers and against drugs of whatever kind wherever, whenever and however we can. "

Sarkozy is telling the youth of France that heroin is a safe as cannabis.
See
2003: Major Developments Scheduled for Year. Things to Look Out For and Things to Look Forward To.

So will France look to Holland to learn from its lower rate of cannabis by youth? Of course not! Instead, they will replace jail sentences, which are rarely imposed, with fines of up to $1,500. So much for liberty, equality and fraternity. Now it is just for the rich.

Contrary to claims by President Jacques Chirac, most of the cannabis in France does not come from Holland, but is brought from North Africa by members of the large Moroccan and Algerian communities, who live in wretched slums. Police have complained that they are being outsmarted by smugglers using hi-tech communications and fast cars.
See
Foreign Affairs Pushes The Party Line At the Highest Levels:
Anti-Dutch Prohibitionist Propaganda for the Elites.April's Reefer Madness Award Winner

Speaking of Holland

The Dutch coalition government, which is already very unpopular, is harassing the coffee shops. There is talk of banning the police from going to coffee shops or smoking cannabis even when they are off duty. There has also been talk of limiting THC levels to 6%. The shop owners are thinking about suing the government, but I predict that nothing will really happen. The Dutch economy is in a recession, after many years of strong growth. The prisons are overcrowded by Dutch standards and there is a serious problem with crime in the immigrant communities. Moreover, the coffee shop system is controlled at the local level, not by the national government. Nonetheless, it is sad that even some Dutch politicians are so dumb that they don't realize how much better their system works
See
Good News From Holland Is Even Better in Context. Large Majority of Dutch Parliament Favors Legalization of Cannabis. Most EU Countries Recognize Dutch Model Superior to DEAland's. We Are Winning!

But for the really, really tragic, Africa is the latest victim of DEAland reefer madness.
See
The UN Commission on Narcotic Drugs Resolution on the Control of Cannabis in Africa. UN Narks Urge War on Poorest of the Poor. Cannabis Prohibition Does Most Damage In Poor Countries.

Recently, Mapinc.org has carried a number of stories from Africa showing the pernicious influence of prohibitionist propaganda on the poorest countries. The latest, SMOKING MARIJUANA IS CRIMINAL, from Uganda has the following gems:

Smoking marijuana is not only criminal but also contributes to commission of other crimes.

According to the head of anti-narcotics unit at CID headquarters, Mr Micheal Were: " A big number of crimes result from the influence of marijuana. "

According to Were, marijuana gives Dutch courage to people who inhale it.

Body builders commonly known as Kanyamas are notorious for smoking marijuana because it gives them courage to way lay people in the city, particularly in the morning and evening.

Crimes that arise out of marijuana influence include waylaying women at night, raping them and defiling young girls.

The drug also contributes to mental breakdown. Some people have run mad due to over inhaling marijuana.

As with so much else about cannabis prohibition, this would be hilarious if it were not so tragic. We are winning, but there will be many more victims before this war on freedom is over.
